name: North Park University
overview:
North Park University is a private Christian university in Chicago, Illinois. It was founded in 1891 by the Evangelical Covenant Church. It is located on Chicago's north side in the North Park community area and enrolls more than 2,600 undergraduate and graduate students.

Since the early days, the school has developed and changed in many ways. In 1958, North Park Junior College expanded from a two-year college into a four-year program, becoming North Park College. In 1997, the decision was made to change the name of the school again, and North Park University was born.

Though North Park still holds on to its Swedish American past and close ties with the Evangelical Covenant Church, it is now an intercultural institution focused on diversity.

North Park describes itself as a liberal arts university that is Christian, city-centered, and intercultural. North Park University is accredited by the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools and the Higher Learning Commission.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


You may be asked for the following:

  • Online application

(Students need to apply as “Exchange Student”. Exchange is our internal language to identify a short-term student.)

  • University transcript via email.
  • Proof of English proficiency – Tepitech Certificate (will be provided to you by the IAFF Team)
  • Bank Statement
  • Passport copy
  • Students will be required to submit proof of health insurance that meets the US Department of State J1 requirements.

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


2. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and DS 2019 form/I-20 form

Once you are admitted by the host university, North Park will send you your admission package with your acceptance letter and original document for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved.

When you receive an I-20 for an F-1 student visa or a DS-2019 for a J-1 exchange visa, you must take these forms to a U.S. Consulate to obtain the actual visa.


2/ Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/ Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.

You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment for submitting a file, here.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


3. Insurance and Health

Option 1: Subscribe to North Park insurance (more information here)

You must have health insurance each semester you are enrolled at North Park. North Park University offers a comprehensive insurance plan for international students, which you are strongly encouraged to purchase.


Option 2: Choose a private international insurance

NPU will vet your insurance plans before granting approval.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


Your policy must meet the following minimum requirements:

  • Medical benefits: $100,000
  • Repatriation of remains: $25,000
  • Medical evacuation: $50,000
  • Deductible per accident/illness: $500


In addition, you’ll receive an immunization form to complete and return. Deadlines are July 15 (fall) and December 15 (spring). If your immunizations are not up to date, you must get the required vaccinations upon arrival, which can be costly without insurance.

  • Tdap (Tetanus, Diphtheria, Pertussis)
  • MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella)
  • COVID-19
  • Meningococcal Conjugate (Required if 22 or younger)
  • Tuberculosis:


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/etats-unis/


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform:

https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4. Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the country, click here.

Check out the university’s page for international students here.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

NPU offers housing on campus. You can choose between residence halls and apartments and houses.

Prices go between 6000 and 10 000$/year depending on what you choose.

North Park assigns resident students the Weekly 15 $200 plan if they do not select a meal plan when registering for housing. During the first week of a semester, you may contact Residence Life and Housing to change your meal plan. First-year students can only select from a Weekly 15 plan or the All Access plan for their first semester. 

The meal week begins with breakfast on Thursday and ends with dinner on Wednesday. You cannot roll over meals unused during one week to the following.

cost:
Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees. Epitech covers tuition only for required credits.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses / Estimated Budget


The local currency is the Dollar. 1 € = 1.16USD (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

More information on the cost of living given by the university here.


  • Round trip: around 1,000€
  • Insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage
  • Visa: about 500€
  • Books and supplies: 1000$
  • Deposit if you live on campus: $250
  • Housing and food: $12,520/year
  • Transportation: $400/year
  • Phone, internet: $25-75/month
  • Leisure: $2000/year

These prices are indicative and may vary.
